message.reasoning:
Let me evaluate against criteria.

C1 Introduction: mission concept (coral reef monitoring, fluid lensing), why needed, one spacecraft with justification, users — operator and customers? It says "operated and accessed from Australia ground facilities" and mentions marine/conservation scientists as beneficiaries. Users not explicitly detailed (operator = University of Tasmania? customers = scientists). Partially addressed. References present. Adequate-to-accomplished. I'd say 7? Users not clearly identified (operator and customers). Some requirements addressed well, others vague. Adequate: 5-6. I'd give 6.

C2 Mission design: launch (Vega E from Kourou), orbit (SSO 600km, i=87.79°, elements table), maneuvers (only EOL), ground control (Mt Pleasant, STK access report), comms frequency (access table, ~20 min mean), mission duration 5 years, EOL drag sail. STK screenshots included (Images 1-5), access summary table. Software files? Not mentioned explicitly in appendix — deliverable R10 requires STK files; screenshots present but files not stated. Technical issues: Kourou latitude stated as 45.05°N — actually Kourou is at ~5.05°N; that's a significant error (typo). Also "A very high altitude would yield low resolution images which is also desirable" — contradictory (should be "not desirable"). Inclination 87.79° at 600 km — check: sun-sync at 600km requires ~97.8°, not 87.79°. The plot shows ~97.9 at 600km, but text says 87.7924° — inconsistent with their own figure! That's a technical error. Also retrograde claim: 87.79° would be prograde; retrograde requires >90°. The plot shows ~97.9 which is retrograde and correct for sun-sync at 600km. So the text value 87.79° is wrong (or a typo), and the table uses 87.79°. Also RAAN 27.33° "indicates location of launch facility" — questionable. Semi-major axis 7171 km correct. Also "an average contact duration of almost twenty minutes" — mean 580.786 s ≈ 9.7 min, not 20 min. Error. Also "The satellite will be recording data in the descending part of its orbit... constantly in sunlight" — descending node for a dawn-dusk? Ambiguous. Also "sun-synchronous orbit inherently experiences significant J2 perturbations as a result of its highly polar inclination" — J2 nodal precession, fine-ish.

Also "latitude of 45.05°N" for Kourou — wrong (5.05°N). And claim "As this is smaller than the target inclination... two launch windows per day" — logic odd.

Despite errors, major requirements addressed with STK evidence. Level: Adequate (4-6) due to errors and inconsistencies. Give 6? The inclination error is significant but the figure shows correct value; the report is comprehensive. I'd give 6.

C3 Conclusion: summarizes findings, notes risks (Vega E not built). Some detail. Adequate-to-accomplished. Give 7? It's fairly specific, ties to evidence. I'd say 7.

C4 Presentation: structure clear, headings, exec summary, figures labeled? Figures have captions like "STK 3D view of orbit: 12 hours apart" but no figure numbers ("Figure 1"). Tables not numbered. References cited [1]-[10] in text mostly; bibliography is bare URLs, includes Wikipedia [6] which is not acceptable per task. Some grammar issues ("which is also desirable", "for the purposed of this satellite", "current owned"). Adequate: 5.

Requirements:
R1 yes (Introduction).
R2 yes (one satellite justified).
R3 partial (users: scientists implied, operator vague).
R4 yes (Vega E, Kourou).
R5 yes (SSO, elements table) — though inclination value error.
R6 yes (no maneuvers except EOL).
R7 yes (Mt Pleasant, access table).
R8 yes (5 years, drag sail EOL).
R9 yes (STK used).
R10 partial (screenshots yes; STK files not mentioned).
R11 partial (structure good, but Wikipedia cited, figure numbering inconsistent).

Technical issues list: Kourou latitude 45.05°N (should be ~5°N); inclination 87.79° inconsistent with sun-sync requirement (~97.8°) and own plot; "average contact duration of almost twenty minutes" vs 580.8 s mean (~9.7 min); "very high altitude would yield low resolution images which is also desirable" contradiction; RAAN 27.33° justification weak; Wikipedia used as reference [6]; figure/table numbering absent.

Overall: solid concept with STK evidence but several technical inconsistencies.
